Prevention: Remove fallen fruit and destroy/ bury as the larvae and pupae are found within the fruit
Monitoring: Look for ‘shot gun’ holes in the leaves and brown/black necrotic areas on fruit.
Twig dieback especially at the growing tips (young shoots).
Small grey weevil which curls up and falls when disturbed.
Yellow eggs laid within fruit, blossoms and young shoots and sealed by adult.
Larvae hatch and feed on the seed where they pupate in the maturing fruit.
Action is required when holes are seen in the leaves at flushing and at blossoming.
Direct Control: Remove fallen fruit and destroy/ bury
Prune dead areas/damaged tips as the larvae are often inside.
Spray at flushing, then blossoming and one week later
Restrictions: Try to avoid spraying pollinators (consider spraying at night)
Protective clothing to be worn when handling pesticides
Re-entry interval 24hrs, Pre harvest interval 3 days
Fipronil. (Regent, Flip, Mortel) ½ tsp/ gal.
